short: The ordinary double point volume gap

title.title: The ordinary double point volume gap
title.subtitle: Claim: a singular klt point of an $n$-fold has normalized volume at most $2(n-1)^n$, equal only at an ODP

plain: A smooth point is the 'biggest' kind; the claim is that the next biggest is always the simple cone $x_0^2+\dots+x_n^2=0$

object.axisLabel: normalized volume $\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X)$ of a point on a fourfold, $n = 4$

beats.text: Smooth points have the largest normalized volume, $n^n$
The claim: every singular klt point sits at or below the ordinary double point
Shown for $n = 4$; the claim covers every dimension $n \ge 2$

steps: First prove the four-dimensional case on its own
Then deduce each dimension from the one below
So the gap holds in every dimension

achievement.label: Spotti–Sun conjecture (2017)
achievement.context: Before: dimension 3 (Liu–Xu, 2019); dimensions 4 and up open
achievement.note: Equality only at the ordinary double point; zero boundary only

verify.detail: No Lean; the every-dimension proof inducts from a separately proved fourfold case
verify.ourCheck: We graded the claim, not whether it is right

voice.text: Smooth points have the largest normalized volume; singular points sit below a gap.
Prove dimension four on its own, then deduce each dimension from the one below.
Claimed: the Spotti-Sun conjecture, in every dimension.

sources.quote: the normalized volume vol̂(x,X) ≤ 2(n−1)^n, with equality iff the analytic germ is an ordinary double point
Liu–Xu (Duke 2019, 'K-stability of cubic threefolds') proved dimension 3 in general. Dimensions ≥ 4 were open.
The proof is an induction on dimension starting from a separately proved fourfold case.
I graded what each family claims, not whether it is right.
